significance: A ruined seaside monastery among the dunes at Pottuvil, held to have been founded more than two thousand years ago by King Kavan Tissa of Ruhuna. Remains of stupas, a seema malaka, an avasa geya and stone images of the Buddha and of kings or gods still stand on the site.
story: The Rajavaliya tells that Devi, daughter of the king of Kelaniya, was set adrift in a golden vessel to appease the sea gods and came ashore here, later marrying Kavan Tissa as Queen Viharamahadevi.
